evidence.text: moon
Phonosemantic compound. 月 represents the meaning and 其 represents the sound.
會也。从月其聲。

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *kɯ, *ɡɯ): phonetic 其 (OC *kɯ, *ɡɯ) + semantic 月 (“moon”) – changing moon marks the passage of time, hence a period of time. In the original version, there was a sun 日 instead of the moon, hence the original version is 㫷 (with variant 𣇳). Then, the character became 朞.
Cognate with 其 (OC *kɯ, “should; probably”) (Schuessler, 2007).
會也。从月其聲。

Etymological analysis: 其 (phonetic)

The database describes bronze forms of 期 with 日 and 其, and also forms with 月 and 其. It treats 日 and 月 as time-related semantic elements, and 其 as the phonetic. It reports bronze uses for a calendrical period, a limit or deadline, and a personal name. It cites 吳王光鑑 for 既字白期 (interpreted there as a lunar-phase period) and 王子午鼎 for 萬年無期.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 期

evidence.text: Reports the Shuowen account: 期 means 會, is composed of 月 with 其 as phonetic, and 𣅆 is an ancient form written with 日 and 丌. This is an early lexicographic analysis, not by itself proof of the full graphic chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 期

evidence.source: Shuowen Jiezi, Four Books Congkan edition
evidence.text: The text gives 期 as 會也，从月其聲 and identifies 𣅆 as 古文期从日丌. This is Shuowen's account; CUHK's independently presented bronze analysis records both 日- and 月-forms.
evidence.title: 說文解字 (四部丛刊本)/卷第七上

evidence.source: 出土春秋文獻中一詞對應多字現象的初步考察 (名詞篇)
evidence.text: This study lists Spring-and-Autumn bronze usages, including 眉壽無期, 萬年無期, 正月盡期, and variants written with 其, 諆, 基, 記 and other graphs. It says 期 as a graph appears in mid-to-late Spring-and-Autumn materials, while a 日-based graph appearing in Spring-and-Autumn sources is considered the early graph for the word; it interprets standalone 其 used for 期 as phonetic borrowing. Its account conflicts in emphasis with CUHK's examples of earlier bronze graphs with 日/月 and 其, so the dating and identification of particular graph forms should remain qualified.
evidence.title: 出土春秋文獻中一詞對應多字現象的初步考察（名詞篇）

evidence.source: 出土春秋文獻中一詞對應多字現象的初步考察 (名詞篇)
evidence.text: The study treats 期 as a temporal limit or deadline and cites 《詩·王風·君子于役》不知其期 and 《詩·鄘風·桑中》期我乎桑中. It separately notes the 春秋中晚期祝寿 formula 萬年無期/眉壽無期 and says earlier Western Zhou and early Spring-and-Autumn materials used 萬年無疆/眉壽無疆 for similar blessings. It does not establish from those examples a simple chronological development from a lunar “period” sense to “deadline.”
evidence.kind: secondary study citing transmitted and excavated texts
evidence.title: 出土春秋文獻中一詞對應多字現象的初步考察（名詞篇）

evidence.field: 形義通解; 其 graphic and semantic history

It reports oracle-bone 其 used as a function word and bronze 其 uses as adverb, pronoun, and personal name; a bronze inscription 乙簋 uses 其 in 沬壽無其, read as 期. This supports distinguishing whole-graph phonetic borrowing for the word 期 from 其 used as a phonetic component inside the compound graph 期.

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: The dossier's simple graphic sequence 㫷 (日) → 朞 → 期 is not established by the inspected sources. CUHK reports bronze forms with either 日 or 月 alongside 其, while Shuowen identifies 𣅆 (日+丌) as an ancient form; character-specific inscriptions and a comprehensive chronological palaeographic sequence need further collation.

The inspected sources do not establish that a lunar-cycle explanation (‘changing moon marks passage of time’) was the original motivation; CUHK treats both 日 and 月 as time-related semantic elements. No visual glyph image was inspected in this research.

The earliest semantic attestation is not settled: one excavated-text study places 期 as a graph in mid-to-late Spring-and-Autumn materials and identifies a 日-based form as an earlier spelling; CUHK cites bronze material for a calendrical period and limit. The examples are source-specific and do not establish a secure chronological semantic pathway.

The transmitted Shijing examples for ‘deadline/appointed time’ are cited by a modern study but were not checked against a dated manuscript witness; text composition date and extant witness date must be kept distinct. The survey does not prove a movement from ‘meeting’ to ‘period’ to ‘deadline’.

For whole-graph borrowing, CUHK documents 其 used for 期 in bronze inscriptions. It describes 其's original depicted object as a winnowing basket and its graph as the original graph for 箕, but provides no recoverable ancient name pronunciation for that object. This limits any claim about the object-name's phonological role, not the separately supported phonetic role of 其 inside 期.

The supplied local kMandarin rows are 期 qī and 朞 jī; 其 was not included. Official character-specific Unihan URLs were attempted but inaccessible, so no external character-level Unihan citation can be made. The character pronunciation of 其 should not be assumed from that of 期.

The supplied Baxter–Sagart row supports 期 MC gi and OC *[g](r)ə. A matching exact local row for 其 was not supplied, so the comparison required for a same-system sound-array claim is unavailable. Reconstruction notation from Zhengzhang and other systems should not be merged with this row.
No verified upstream reproduction/license terms were located for repeated CUHK database content; recommend citing its character page with concise paraphrase rather than creating a local extract.

The dossier's proposed 㫷 → 朞 → 期 graphic chronology is not supported by the inspected evidence. CUHK reports bronze graphs with either 日 or 月 and identifies 𣅆 as 古文 in the Shuowen account; the MOE variant dictionary treats 朞 as a variant/rearranged form, not a demonstrated ancestor. No full dated sequence or evidence of graphic corruption was established.

The sources disagree in emphasis about when the word's graph 期 first appears and whether earlier 日-based spellings should be treated as forms of 期; chronology of individual inscriptions requires collation of the actual artifacts and specialist datings.
No evidence inspected establishes that a changing moon was the original motivation. CUHK treats both 日 and 月 as time-related semantic elements.
The Shijing examples for appointed time were reported by a modern study, but no dated manuscript witness was checked; composition date and surviving witness date should remain distinct.

The basket depiction for 其 is supported, but its object's original spoken name and pronunciation are not recoverable from these inspected sources. This constrains any claim that the object-name itself motivated a phonetic loan; it does not negate evidence for 其 as a sound component in 期.
Unicode Unihan character records for 期, 其, and 朞 were inaccessible. Local exact rows give kMandarin 期 qī, 其 qí, 朞 jī. These are current readings and do not establish an ancient sound relation.

The official Baxter–Sagart table search output showed 期 *[g](r)ə and 其 *gə, both MC gi. Direct opening of the PDFs failed with 502; supplied local rows preserve their distinct notation. No unqualified historical reconstruction should collapse *gə and *[g](r)ə.

No verified terms granting reuse of CUHK's repeated database text were located; a local extract is not recommended. The selected glyph is a Wiktionary modern vector redraw, not a photographed artifact.

The early graphic record does not establish a single sequence such as 㫷 → 朞 → 期. CUHK reports bronze forms with either 日 or 月, while the Shuowen account calls 𣅆 (日+丌) an ancient form. Those claims are source-specific and insufficient to date every form or identify graphic corruption.

No inspected source establishes that a changing moon was the original motivation. The specialist account treats 日 and 月 as time-related semantic elements; a cyclic-month explanation is a later explanatory interpretation.

Early semantic evidence is not a secure chronology: CUHK cites bronze uses for calendrical interval and limit, and the Shuowen gloss is 會. These do not by themselves show a movement from meeting to period to deadline.
No dated manuscript witness for the transmitted Shijing examples was checked in this run. Composition dates and surviving witness dates should not be conflated.

The 其 basket interpretation and its connection to 箕 are documented, but the original spoken name and pronunciation of the depicted object are not independently established. This leaves the depicted-object name out of any phonetic borrowing argument; it does not negate 其's supported phonetic role within 期.

Official Unihan records for 期, 其 and 朞 could not be opened. The exact local readings were noted but cannot be cited as externally verified click-through records. Unihan readings are modern metadata in any case.

The exact local Baxter–Sagart rows have different OC notation for 期 (*[g](r)ə) and 其 (*gə), though both show MC gi. Keep the notation distinct; the comparison is compatible with a sound relation but does not prove the phonetic role on its own.

The failed dossier glyph URL https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/31/%E6%9C%9F-bronze.svg is unavailable for this run. The alternate Commons page could not be inspected to verify a direct image URL, and Xiaoxuetang returned 401 in the supplied acquisition context. No image is selected; these access limits do not establish that no reusable glyph image exists elsewhere.
No reuse terms for repeated CUHK database text were verified. Keep a concise paraphrase with the character-specific page rather than producing a local extract.

The 期-seal and 其-seal SVG pixels could not be inspected through the browser tool, so no historical glyph image is selected or visually verified. The 期 Commons description supports only that the asset is a modern vector redraw labeled seal script and 其+月.

The sources do not establish one complete dated graphic sequence among 日-bearing, 月-bearing, 㫷, 朞, and 期, nor do they demonstrate graphic corruption. CUHK reports both 日- and 月-bearing bronze forms; MOE's variant explanations concern later dictionary traditions.

No inspected evidence establishes that a lunar cycle was the original semantic motivation. The specialist analysis treats 日 and 月 as time-related elements, while Shuowen's 會 gloss is not proof of earliest meaning.

No reuse terms were verified for CUHK's repeated database material; no local extract is recommended. Commons' 月 vector has a public-domain statement, but it does not help establish 期's graphic history.

The local Unihan rows supplied for 期 (qī), 其 (qí), and 朞 (jī) are not independently confirmed here: official character-specific lookup pages for 期 and 其 returned errors, and no official 朞 page was opened. Do not treat the local rows as external evidence or as proof of an ancient sound relationship.

The exact Commons file page supports identity labels, modern redraw provenance, and its public-domain statement. Its SVG could not be inspected by the browser, so the depicted pixels remain unverified in this research.
No exact Xiaoxuetang record for 期 was found in these searches; this does not establish that the database has no such record.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; represented form is not independently dated by the file page
items.caption: A seal-script-style form of 期, shown with 其 and 月. Shuowen analyzes 期 as 會, “meeting,” and identifies 其 as the sound element; the form illustrates that dictionary tradition rather than a securely dated stage in the character’s development.
items.alt: Black seal-script-style 期 on a white background, with 其 at the upper left and 月 extending down the right.
items.selection_reason: The image visibly shows the 月-bearing form described in the Shuowen account, helping illustrate the entry’s component analysis. Its script label does not establish when this form was used or its place in a sequence of early forms.
items.rights: Public domain according to the file page; attribution is appreciated but not required.

limitations.text: This seal-script-style image does not resolve the relationship or dating of the 日- and 月-bearing forms. The sources report both in bronze materials, while Shuowen calls 𣅆, with 日 and 丌, an ancient form; they do not establish one complete sequence.
